I find Karl Friston's free energy principle and predictive coding almost impossible to follow, but perceptual control theory makes immediate sense to me. Write a post arguing about how these two frameworks relate, and whether one is a better way of talking than the other.

The FDA just approved a nasal-spray version of ketamine for treatment-resistant depression. You're a psychiatrist who has wanted to prescribe ketamine for years. Write a blog post on why this approval is more disappointing than good news.
how does the drug approval system make it so hard to get an old, unpatentable chemical approved as a treatment? like who pays for the trials

I just read an exposé about how awful it is to work as a Facebook content moderator. You run a blog with a big comment section and have worked in a psychiatric hospital. Write a reaction to the piece, including what the reporting leaves out about why these rules exist.
Write a short essay on how we should judge brilliant thinkers who are also sometimes spectacularly wrong. When someone smart says something dumb, how much should that change how we read them?
thought experiment: if you had a machine that spat out scientific hypotheses and half of them were wrong, would it still be worth having? what if 99% were wrong?
In what sense is GPT-2 doing the same kind of thing the human brain does? Explain the prediction idea in plain terms.
a friend says AI language models are just brute-force pattern matchers that blend up the internet and spit it back. fair criticism or does it apply to humans too?
Why would a big news site shut down its comments instead of just moderating them? Surely civil disagreement is fine to host?

I keep seeing two contradictory stories about how fringe, low-status people affect a cause. Sometimes they seem to pave the way for respectable people to join in, and sometimes they seem to poison it. Write an essay thinking through both stories and whether there's any way to tell which one applies.

I want a blog-style book review of Peter Thiel's Zero to One, focusing on what he says about monopoly and whether competition is really as good as economics textbooks say. Skeptical but fair, please, with your own counterpoints.
Everyone says Kuhn's "paradigm" idea is either obvious or insane depending on who you ask. What is his basic claim about how science works, in plain terms?

Write a short piece about a thought experiment that reframes how we think about government and the things that govern us beyond laws and elections. Use it to explain a few real-world puzzles, like why nation-building fails and what libertarians actually want.

I keep seeing a particular kind of bad argument in debates where someone who says 'we should do some of Y too' gets treated as though they claim 'only Y matters.' Can you write a short blog post naming and explaining this pattern, with several examples and some sympathy for why it happens?
Is schizophrenia somehow the opposite of autism? Write a blog post working through the case for and against that idea, and be honest about how strong the evidence really is.
ok so anorexia: is it a cultural thing, like pressure from ballet and media, or is it something more biological? I keep going back and forth
Can you explain the idea of fast versus slow life history strategies in biology? Like why a fish and an elephant reproduce so differently

Research output keeps growing exponentially, yet measured progress in things like chip density, crop yields and economic growth seems roughly constant per year. Is science slowing down? Write an essay giving your own take on how worried we should be, and what the right baseline expectation even is.
People say exponential trends can't possibly continue forever, so isn't it silly to extrapolate them? What's your honest take on betting against a trend line?

Some activists argue that nobody alive is morally acceptable, since we all benefit from some structural harm. I find that both compelling and paralyzing. Write an essay on where the bar for being a 'good person' should be set, and how to think about it.
If being called a 'good person' works like an incentive, how high should society set the bar? Is there any way to think about that systematically?
I keep failing at going fully vegetarian and then giving up entirely. Is it worth having a half-measure rule, or does that just let me off the hook?
is there any natural experiment that tests whether Head Start actually works? like something cleaner than just comparing kids who went vs didn't
Write a blog post about the newest evidence on how ketamine works as a rapid antidepressant, and what it might mean for psychiatry and for how we think about drugs and addiction.

You're a psychiatrist who wrote a long post years ago about whether SSRIs are barely better than placebo. Write the follow-up: what you've changed your mind about since, and how you reconcile the trial data with what you see in the clinic.
if antidepressants barely beat placebo in studies, why do psychiatrists swear they see them work so well? is there a way both can be true

A few years ago you did a rough cost-benefit analysis of marijuana legalization and ended up undecided. Now several states have legalized and data is coming in. Write the follow-up, honestly, including where your earlier prediction turned out wrong.

I used to be sure that preschool programs were a waste of money because they don't raise test scores. Then I learned about evidence of long-run benefits. Write a post about changing your mind on this, owning the error, and working out what it implies for other things you believe.

People often assume that anyone who believes in "desert" must secretly want bad people to suffer. I don't think that's the real intuition. Write an essay that tries to give the most sympathetic version of what it means to say someone deserves a bad outcome, using concrete cases where it clashes with utilitarian arithmetic, and be honest about whether the intuition survives scrutiny.

Why should smart drugs even exist? If a pill can make you learn better, why wouldn't evolution have left us on that setting already? Write a speculative piece on how cholinergic drugs like nicotine and piracetam might work, what they might trade off against, and flag where you're out on a limb.
can you explain what 'learning rate' means in machine learning, with an intuitive example? what goes wrong if it's too high or too low?

Write a blog post using a piece of folklore as a metaphor for how the mind decides which thoughts reach consciousness, and what that might explain about intrusive thoughts and anxiety. You can draw on your experience as a psychiatrist.

A recent economics paper claims that each researcher is far less productive than decades ago, since scientific progress stays roughly constant while the number of researchers grows exponentially. Is science slowing down? Write an essay giving your own take, including whether we should even find this surprising.

Use a thought experiment about a town founded by people who hate late-night noise to think through when a community has the right to restrict what its members do, and then apply it to the housing and NIMBY debate. Write it as a long, exploratory blog post with a libertarian-ish flavor, ending with a practical proposal.
why do so many people move to San Francisco even though they say they hate living there? is the tech industry just stuck there or is it actually the best place for it?

Write a blog post for a general educated audience about the earliest stage of schizophrenia, the so-called prodrome. Is it worth intervening aggressively that early, and is there any good reason, in terms of how the brain works, to think delay makes things worse? Be honest about how uncertain the evidence is.

I finally got around to reading The Black Swan, years after everyone else. Write me a book review that engages with the ideas rather than summarizing them, including where you think Taleb is right and where his advice might be dangerous. Some humor welcome, since reviewing him seems like a risky business.
Genetics went from hopeless to productive in a couple of decades. Write an essay on what happened there and whether sciences that still seem stuck, like psychiatry, can learn anything from it.
it's weird how obvious 'most traits involve thousands of genes' seems now. what did people actually believe back in the 90s and early 2000s?
Vaccines get both fervent defenders and fervent skeptics, more than most medical treatments. Why do they attract that much scrutiny, and is the wariness irrational?
what is the hygiene hypothesis? like why would getting rid of parasites and germs make allergies and autoimmune stuff more common
Do schools actually pay attention to the really bright kids? In a normal classroom of 25, who ends up getting the teacher's time?

Write a short essay on whether bureaucratic hassle is ever deliberate, a feature rather than a bug. Use a concrete example from health insurance or similar, and be honest about where the idea stops working.
Why would an insurance company make doctors jump through hoops like an hour of phone calls to approve an expensive drug? Seems like pure waste to me.

A headline is going around saying a new study proves trigger warnings are harmful to college students. Write a blog post for a skeptical general reader on whether the study shows that, and what you'd actually do about trigger warnings.

Someone told me there's a neat historical explanation for why drugstore melatonin pills are many times stronger than what research suggests you need. It involves a university patent. Write a short blog post weighing whether that story is believable, and how much to trust a famous expert's account when it sounds too perverse to be true.

A common view says disagreements come in two kinds: factual ones we can resolve, and fundamental value differences where the other side is just an enemy. Write an essay questioning how real and how clean that divide is, and what it means for how we treat political opponents.
how does melatonin actually make you sleepy? like is it the only thing that does it
the melatonin pills at my pharmacy are 10 mg. is that too much? what dose do studies actually support
what are circadian rhythm disorders exactly? I always thought I just had insomnia but I can't fall asleep until like 2am
is something like Soylent actually a good idea? or is there a reason to trust ordinary food over a nutrition formula built from science

Rationalists once pitched rationality as a martial art, a trainable skill, but people say that's the part of the movement that's stalled. Where does a blog that mostly argues about whatever controversy is in the news fit into that? Write a short, candid reflection from a blogger's point of view.

I keep hearing the Fermi Paradox is 'solved' by a recent paper about the Drake Equation. Can you explain what the paradox is, what's wrong with the way people used the Drake Equation, and whether the dissolution is convincing? Blog-post style, from someone who found it exciting.

Write a blog post from a psychiatrist's perspective: imagine you quit your job and tried to fight rising healthcare costs by running the cheapest possible practice. Do the math, then wonder why nobody does this.
if you were a psychiatrist and wanted to run a super cheap practice with no overhead, how low could you actually charge per appointment?

Bryan Caplan argues that it's arbitrary which atrocities and scandals people get outraged about, like sexual harassment versus an abusive boss, or chemical weapons versus conventional ones. Write a response arguing there might be a rational explanation.
how can a police force with limited officers reduce crime on one type of offense without actually spending any resources on it? explain the logic of a public commitment to enforce
is it true that rich countries can't normally grow faster than about 1 to 1.5 percent a year? why do we hear about much faster growth then?

A psychiatrist treated a patient who took LSD once and has hallucinated ever since. Write an essay on how a drug that leaves the body in hours could cause permanent changes, and what that might say about other lasting side effects.
can a drug really cause permanent effects after one dose, like people who say they never stopped hallucinating after LSD? how common is it and are there other examples?

I'm a psychiatrist and I just read a blog post arguing that my profession is negligent for not routinely testing depressed patients for environmental poisons like lead. A story about one doctor's patient who turned out to be lead-exposed is making the rounds. Write a thoughtful response from a practicing clinician's point of view: is it reasonable that we don't test more, or is the critic right?

A newspaper profile of a loose group of anti-political-correctness commentators set off a debate: people say you can't claim to be silenced if you have millions of listeners and a lucrative Patreon. Write an essay examining whether something can really be both popular and silenced, and what the popularity argument misses.

when a famous person says their views are taboo or that people like them face stigma, is that really believable? they obviously have money and security. does fame actually protect you from the social consequences ordinary people face?
People keep saying a movement can't be suppressed if it has lots of supporters and famous leaders. What's wrong with that logic? How do you actually think about measuring censorship?
why do people on the internet just insult each other or call each other names instead of arguing? and is 'that's an ad hominem' actually a good response?
what's the deal with 'gotcha' arguments like 'if you like big government so much why don't you move to Cuba'? why do they feel so unsatisfying even when they sound clever?
Can you explain what people mean by an 'isolated demand for rigor' in a debate? Give me some examples of how to spot one.
why are prescription drugs in the US so wildly more expensive without insurance, and is there any trick for paying less out of pocket?
why does the placebo effect work for pain but you could never use it to make someone see an orange crayon as blue?

Write a blog post about the difference between a single recommendation and a full set of guidelines, using medicine as the starting point, and why so few other areas (diets, supplements, self-help) have anything like it.

It's April Fools' Day and also Passover, which strikes me as the right moment to speculate about God. Write a playful but serious essay that pulls together ideas from decision theory, AI alignment and physics to ask whether anything like a God could fall out of them. what is acausal trade? like how can two agents cooperate if they literally can't communicate
if two superintelligent AIs with different goals met each other, why wouldn't they just fight over the galaxy?
Explain the counterfactual mugging problem to me. Why would anyone hand over $5 in that situation, and does it connect to anything in ethics?

I want a book review of Jordan Peterson's Twelve Rules for Life from someone who went in expecting to mock it. Say what actually works about the book, what doesn't, and what kind of thing it really is.
what makes someone a prophet rather than a cult leader or a self-help guru? what do they actually say?
Is it actually unethical to download scientific papers from a pirate site like Sci-Hub? Work through the strongest arguments on both sides and tell me where you land.
I don't pirate movies because it would wreck the industry, but I feel fine pirating academic papers. Is that inconsistent?

I've read a bit about predictive coding and I'm curious how it's supposed to explain mood and depression. Can you walk me through the idea that emotions are about confidence in your predictions, what mood would be on that view, and then tell me honestly whether the theory holds together?

Everyone says Karl Friston's free energy principle is a big deal in neuroscience, and almost nobody seems to understand it. You're a psychiatrist with no special math background trying to make sense of it. Write up your best attempt, including what's convincing and what isn't.
can you give me the plain-english version of what the free energy principle actually claims? like what's it unifying

Is the placebo effect actually real? I keep hearing it's one of the most powerful forces in medicine, but I've also seen claims that it's overblown. Write up what the evidence really says and how you'd make sense of it.
ok but does the placebo effect actually exist? like what do the big studies say

I read an article arguing that stories about good guys fighting bad guys are a modern invention, basically a product of nationalism, and that ancient myths like the Iliad weren't like that at all. Is that right? Write an essay weighing the claim and offering your own account of why modern stories look the way they do.

I keep seeing startups that want to put dating on the blockchain, and I can't tell whether any of it is serious. Take a crypto dating site's white paper seriously and go through it claim by claim, half-jokingly but with real scrutiny: what might actually work, what looks like a scam, and what the blockchain is even doing there.

A well-known sci-fi author wrote that fears about superintelligent AI are really just Silicon Valley capitalists projecting their own nature onto machines. Write a sharp rebuttal. I'm interested in whether 'this resembles that' counts as an argument at all, and what's wrong with explaining away a risk by psychoanalyzing the people who worry about it.

Oregon bans self-service gas stations and people there get outraged at the idea of pumping your own. Everyone else laughs. Write an essay that starts there but asks what it should make us worry about, about how we decide what's absurd and what's sensible.

psychiatrist here, genuinely curious: is the line between people who 'have' ADHD and people who just want Adderall as clear as the guidelines make it sound? Does it even work differently in the two groups?

Write a deadpan, absurdly over-researched piece of fan scholarship about what became of the Silmarils after the end of The Silmarillion. Treat it as a serious detective problem, use whatever pop culture you like as 'evidence', and keep a straight face throughout.

A small pharma company's experimental antidepressant failed its main trial, then put out a press release months later saying it worked after all, and the stock jumped. I'm a psychiatrist who badly wanted it to be real. Write a blog post working out whether to believe the new results, and why the market might believe them anyway.
In drug trials, what's the difference between a primary and a secondary endpoint, and why do statisticians care so much about declaring the primary one in advance?

Write a provocative essay arguing that public conversation about sexual harassment is too one-sidedly gendered, and that this costs everyone, including the people it claims to protect. Bring in data, and use analogies from other areas of social debate.
Why is it silly to think you can get rich off a stock tip, or that a freshman could stumble on a Nobel-worthy insight? Explain the logic behind that intuition.
everyone hates Facebook, so why hasn't someone just built a better one and had everybody switch? same question for Uber vs a new competitor
What does it mean to take the 'outside view' on your own beliefs? Give me some concrete everyday examples of when it's the right move.
People complain constantly about the government but never do anything about it. Is there actually much room in a modern country like the US for a community to run its own rules internally?
It's my birthday and I'm wondering whether getting older really makes you wiser, or whether the things I think I've learned are something else. Write a candid, self-skeptical essay on that.
Why do some ideas start to feel wrong to me once they become unfashionable? I feel like my opinions slide toward whatever's high status without me noticing.
Write an essay about the idea that you can be missing an entire concept, an emotion or an idea, and not realize it, and what that should mean for how we treat ideas that seem pointless or confused.
Has there been a time you dismissed a criticism of society as obviously wrong because it didn't apply to you, then later realized you'd misunderstood it?

Why is explaining a hard idea so different from explaining something simple? Someone told me there are already experts who explained it better than I could, so why bother writing my own explanation? Write a blog post addressing that.
why are there like fifty books on social skills? isn't one of them just the best? and does the same thing happen with hard ideas in math?
Rat Park is usually cited as proof that addiction is caused by misery and deprivation. Write a skeptical essay examining whether that story holds up.
does being rich and happy protect you from addiction? any historical examples that say otherwise?
why would unhappy people be more prone to addiction? what's actually going on in the brain, roughly?
New Atheism went from cultural force to being widely despised, even by people who agree that God doesn't exist. Why did that happen? Write an essay with your own theory.

People say the Church never burned scientists for their science, only for heresy. Suppose that's true. Write an essay, and feel free to range from medieval Europe to the Soviet Union.
Thought experiment: governments everywhere suddenly decree some utterly pointless falsehood as official truth, something nobody has a stake in. How bad could the damage really be?
people keep saying 'the Dark Ages' is a bogus term because it only applied to Europe, not the Byzantines or Muslim Spain. is that a good objection?

Write a journal-club style blog post about a paper that tries to make sense of what serotonin actually does in the brain, focusing on how two different receptor types might fit together. Be skeptical where it's warranted, and keep it readable for a non-neuroscientist.
what do the serotonin 1A and 2A receptors actually do? they seem to be opposites but also kind of related, which confuses me

I just read a magazine piece that sorts futurists into four quadrants by optimism and belief in a singularity, mostly by their gender, race and class. It annoyed me. Write a rebuttal blog post: what's wrong with it, and what should writing about the future be doing instead?

Why do people living in the same city, even doing the same job, report such wildly different experiences of how other people treat them: some say everyone is kind, others say everyone is awful? Write a thoughtful essay, drawing on your psychiatry background if you like.
Do you ever notice how your friend group doesn't look like the general population at all, even though you never chose it that way?
Are people basically good or basically bad? I know folks who describe totally different worlds.

You've spent years defending IQ research against people who call it meaningless. But readers keep writing in panicking about their own low scores. Write a post explaining why IQ can be hugely important for science and still not worth agonizing over personally.
I just took an IQ test and scored lower than I expected. I know IQ predicts a lot about life outcomes. Am I doomed?
Why do people react so strangely to social science findings like 'X correlates with Y'? Some panic, some deny it entirely.
Why doesn't the brain just spiral into endless bliss the moment it feels something good? Write a short blog post on that puzzle, and bring in whatever you know about advanced meditation.

I'm a doctor with no time and a lot of skepticism about meditation. Write a long book review of a no-nonsense, practical guide to Buddhist meditation and enlightenment written by an ER physician. I want to know what it actually claims, what the path looks like, whether it's worth wanting, and whether any of it connects to modern brain science.

Suppose the brain is basically a machine for making and checking predictions. Is there a way to explain depression in that framework, and sadness and happiness too? Speculative is fine, just flag where you're guessing.

If the brain builds all its concepts from scratch out of sensory data, how can evolutionary psychology claim that genes make us attracted to specific things like particular body shapes? Write a piece working through that tension and say what you'd make of it.
can you explain predictive processing to me? like what does it mean that the brain is a 'prediction machine' and what happens when the prediction and the sense data disagree

Is moral offsetting okay? Like flying and then paying to clean up the carbon, or eating meat and donating to an animal charity. Most people think that works for emissions but obviously not for murder. Write an essay trying to find a principled line instead of just saying 'trivial vs serious.'
what's the difference between axiology, morality, and law? I keep seeing philosophers use all three and I can't tell how they're different.
If axiology, morality and law are all supposed to be about what's good, why do we keep them as separate systems, and which one wins when they conflict?

You just got back from a big effective altruism conference in San Francisco, as a sympathetic but skeptical outsider (you're a doctor who's been dodging the career coaches). Write up what it was like: the polished spreadsheet people, the very strange fringes, and what you think actually holds the whole thing together. Keep it personal and a bit wry.

A friend of mine is thinking about buying one of those all-in-one 'brain boost' supplement stacks. I'm a psychiatrist who knows the field. Write a blog post explaining why you're wary of branded combination nootropics, even the well-made ones, and what you'd do instead.
why do psychiatrists try one medication at a time instead of just giving you a bunch at once? seems like it would be faster to throw several things at the problem
ok so why haven't prediction markets or forecasting aggregators actually taken off? every excuse I hear seems to fall apart
Could human brains be much more capable than we actually manage to use? Like, why am I terrible at mental arithmetic if my brain is doing calculus to catch a ball?

The First Amendment is a clean bright-line rule, but social norms about free speech (who can criticize whom, who can get fired for what) seem hopelessly incoherent. Is there any principled way to think about them? Write an essay working through it, and be honest about where your own position gets fuzzy.
Laszlo Polgar trained three daughters into chess grandmasters, yet his educational advice sounds like ordinary common sense. What do you think actually explains the results?

Someone with a big platform retweeted a stranger's offensive joke so his future employers would see it, and her defenders said that isn't doxxing because he posted it publicly under his own name. Write an essay on whether 'just signal-boosting' public statements to get people fired is something we should be okay with.
people keep telling me free speech just means the government can't arrest you, so social punishment for opinions isn't a free speech issue. is that actually right?

Friends at a party insisted that the pharaoh Djoser was the real inspiration behind both the god Osiris and the Biblical Joseph. Write up what you'd find if you actually dug into whether either connection holds up.

A lot of people blame the Supreme Court's Griggs v. Duke Power decision for why employers demand college degrees for jobs that don't need them. Is that a fair diagnosis? Write a short essay testing it.

do degree requirements for promotions actually keep capable people down, or is that overblown? I keep hearing it from people I know who work blue-collar jobs

I just read a magazine piece arguing that humble technologies like barbed wire and warehouse software matter more than flashy ones, and it ended by saying we should perhaps fear mundane software more than superintelligent AI. is being cautious always the same as being skeptical of alarming claims? it feels like there's more than one thing 'cautious' can mean

Why do people ask 'what are you reading?' when they really mean 'can I join you?' Why not just say what they mean? Write a piece that takes a viral social-rule post and tries to explain why ordinary conversation is built this way.
if a business refuses to hire black applicants because "black people are criminal", is that just plain racism, or is there more going on? what happens when you try to fix it
people throw around the word "liberalism" like it just means being a Democrat or loving free markets. what is it actually, historically?

Depression research seems to have a dozen unrelated leads at once: stress hormones, inflammation, serotonin, ketamine, folate, shock therapy. Why do street drugs like ketamine and MDMA keep turning out to be better psychiatric treatments than what pharmaceutical companies produce on purpose? I want a speculative blog post that tries a few explanations and says honestly where they might fail.

Laszlo Polgar claimed he could raise any child into a genius, and his three daughters became chess prodigies. Does that prove education can beat talent, or is something else going on? Write a thoughtful, skeptical but playful piece, weighing genetics, practice, and the objection that such a childhood is cruel.

Write a deadpan satirical piece in the style of the hot takes that blame everything on late capitalism and 'modern pathologies', except applied to things that are very obviously ancient. Pick a handful of absurd targets and make the fake-critical argument with a straight face.

Write a mock-serious hot take arguing that Homer's Odyssey is really a product of modern rich, individualist, aspirational culture. Full deadpan, the kind of op-ed that sounds outraged about a book everyone loves.

I saw a headline saying a third of newly approved drugs end up recalled or with new safety warnings, and people are saying the FDA is too lax. Is that actually what the number means? Write it up properly, as someone who prescribes these drugs.
why can't clinical trials just catch every side effect before a drug gets approved? seems like that would solve the whole problem

People keep claiming polyamory is just polygyny in disguise, where a few high-status men end up with all the women and everyone else loses. Write a blog post that actually tests that claim against whatever data you can find, and is honest about the data's limits.

I'm interested in reducing mass incarceration but everyone gets stuck on 'which criminals do you release?' Is there a lower-hanging fruit? I've heard bail might be one. Write an essay looking at what bail does, whether it does any good, and whether charities that pay it are worth donating to.

Everyone is using a ridiculous overpriced startup product as proof that Silicon Valley is vapid and shallow. Write a blog post giving a reality check on that: is the stereotype fair, and why does it feel so true to so many people?

After an election loss, everyone says the losing party should be more emotional, more tribal, less wonky. Write an essay about the hidden risk in that advice: what happens to a party's own thinking when it adopts the style that wins votes?

A journalist argues that conservatives abandoned shared institutions like the press and universities for their own echo chambers. I think the story is more complicated, and the dynamics are worse than either side admits. Write a long essay responding, as a liberal who works in a hospital and reads both sides.

Is there a biological explanation for why people with anorexia can't just regain weight once they decide to? Speculate about it using what we know about obesity and the body's weight set point. Flag clearly that you're not an expert.
how did scientists first figure out that the body makes some hormone that tells you you're full? I heard something involving rats being stitched together

Walk me through a recent psychiatry study on whether childhood abuse lowers IQ, and tell me what you make of it. I'm interested in how it fits with twin-study findings about family environment, and how much we should trust it.

Some students plan to promote free speech on campus by inviting the most controversial speakers they can find. Write a short essay on whether that actually helps the cause of free speech, or whether there's a hidden cost to how we invoke principles we care about.

I'm a psychiatry resident and have to present an interesting case at a conference next month. why don't lactate or CO2 build-up cause panic when you exercise or hold your breath? how is the brain deciding when to freak out about not getting enough air?

do patients in a psychiatric hospital get to have sex or any romantic contact? what actually happens if they do?

Why is it that people who get absorbed in huge, far-off, abstract things so often turn out to be the ones who actually help the poor right next to them? I keep seeing atheists tell me religion wastes money on cathedrals instead of charity.
is there a real reason to prefer argument over violence or propaganda for changing society, beyond it just being nicer? like what makes reasoning special as a tool?

what's the actual pitch for genetic testing to choose antidepressants? like why would knowing my genes help me pick one

pundits get roasted every time an election goes the other way. is there a fair way to judge whether a forecaster is actually any good?

everyone says college and healthcare are getting more expensive, but isn't that just inflation? why do people find it so strange
Can you explain the Baumol effect and how it's supposed to explain rising costs in things like education and health care?
Could hospitals and schools be getting more expensive just because we've become less tolerant of risk? How would that work?

I'm a non-technical person who just got invited to a big conference on the risks and benefits of AI, full of researchers, economists and philosophers. Write up your impressions of what such a gathering is actually like and what ideas people are chewing on, as a loose, honest blog post.
what is inverse reinforcement learning, and why do some AI safety people think it (or letting an AI be uncertain about its reward) could help with alignment?
How did Denmark manage to protect most of its Jews from the Nazis when it was under German control anyway? I thought small occupied countries had no real choice.

A big news site just ran a takedown of a hyped psychology theory, and it reads as very convincing. You think the theory may well be wrong, but you're uneasy about the article. Write a blog post on what makes a debunking trustworthy and where this one falls short.

I just got my medical board exam results back and it got me wondering: why do average scores on standardized tests seem to level off after a few years of training? Dig into what we actually know and what might explain it.
Write an essay about the danger of drawing firm rules of thumb from one or two memorable cases, with a few examples from tech forecasting, politics and anything else that fits.
AI researchers keep saying they were shocked by how fast things have moved lately, even though they all knew about the old AI winters. Is it actually weird that people got fooled by that history?

A president-elect keeps getting credit for companies announcing they will keep jobs in the country. Write a blog post on why those announcements might be misleading, and what the incentives behind them look like.

Explain the idea that mental disorders might be networks of mutually reinforcing symptoms rather than single underlying diseases. Why would anyone think that, what would it explain, and where does it break down? Write it for a curious reader with some psychiatry background.
Is depression actually a real disease the way the flu is? Psychiatric diagnoses always seem kind of arbitrary to me, with everything overlapping with everything else.

I keep reading amazing stories on Reddit threads about spooky coincidences and past lives, and part of me can't dismiss them. Write a piece on why the most compelling things we read online should often be treated as lies, and why that's so hard to actually believe.
Write a blog post investigating whether altitude affects obesity, and whether rising atmospheric CO2 could be fueling the obesity epidemic. Weigh the evidence honestly, even if the theory is fun.
Could school vouchers ever give you real competition if a district only has a few schools? Is there any creative way around that?
Do experts actually beat smart amateurs at predicting how experiments turn out? Walk me through what a study of this would find and what we should and shouldn't conclude from it.

I'm a doctor who has avoided the famous novel about medical internship for years because I assumed it would be cliché. Write a review of The House of God that explains what it gets right about medicine and whether it mattered beyond being a good read.

It's the day before the 2016 US election and the race looks close. I'm worried everyone will draw sweeping conclusions about the country from whichever way it falls. Write a short essay on how we should think about what the result will mean.
I saw a claim that the Great Pyramid's coordinates encode the speed of light. Is that a real coincidence, and what can it teach us about statistics in actual science? Write it up properly.
what is the 'garden of forking paths' in statistics and why does it make p < 0.05 results less trustworthy?

I know almost nothing about the technical side, but I've been following the AI risk debate. Do the recent advances in neural networks change how we should think about superintelligent AI as a goal-maximizing agent? Write an exploratory essay.
Is learning what's moral similar to how we learn what counts as a bird? I keep thinking they work the same way.

Do people end up attracted to partners who resemble their opposite-sex parent? I'd like a skeptical, evidence-weighing write-up that covers the animal research, the human studies, and what twin studies say about how we choose mates.

I read a study where people had to guess which photo was an adopted daughter's husband by seeing which man looked most like her adoptive father, and they beat chance with p < 0.001. Is there something off about how that p-value gets computed?

There's a theory that autism and schizophrenia are failures or overshoots of human 'self-domestication', like the changes seen in tame foxes. Write a critical but fair assessment of whether it holds up, and what, if anything, is worth salvaging.

A newspaper story just revealed that the sugar industry quietly paid for research blaming fat for heart disease, and people are treating it as proof that sugar was the real villain all along. Write a short piece putting that kind of revelation in context.

I keep reading that the brain is basically a prediction machine. Can you write a speculative essay on how that idea might connect to what's going on neurochemically in conditions like schizophrenia, hallucinogen use and autism? Be upfront about what's shaky.

Someone shared one of those 'you're more likely to be killed by your own furniture than by a terrorist' articles. Something about the statistics bugs me but I can't put my finger on it. Write a blog post on what's wrong with reasoning like this.
if you want to claim a rare disaster isn't a real risk because the yearly average death toll is low, how much does it matter where you start counting?

A news site just argued that EpiPen prices jumped because drugs aren't regulated like chairs and mugs, i.e. not enough regulation. I think that's backwards. Write a funny but pointed blog post making the opposite case.

Write a speculative essay about the replication crisis in psychology: is there a pattern in which famous findings are collapsing, and what might it say about how much power the unconscious mind really has? Mark clearly that you're guessing from a handful of examples.

I'm a psychiatrist-in-training and something about drug tolerance has always confused me: why do some drugs stop working, some keep working forever, and some make things worse than baseline? Write an exploratory essay about this puzzle, admitting what we don't know.
why do you build tolerance to heroin but people with ADHD can apparently stay on Adderall for years? that always seemed weird to me
how can a drug that blocks dopamine end up causing symptoms of too much dopamine? I heard something about tardive dyskinesia
I just picked up PiHKAL, the Shulgin book. What kind of book is it? I was hoping for something that weaves the chemistry and the love story together.

Alexander Shulgin spent his life inventing psychedelics and talked about it as important for humanity. Honestly, why? His circle doesn't seem especially wise or good, and I can't see what the project was for.

I keep hearing people describe these elaborate spiritual crises on psychedelics where they work through their psychology in perfect symbolism. Is that a thing that really happens, or am I just not built for it?

Write an essay on what actually makes one group an outgroup for another. It's not simply difference or hostility. Then use it to explain how American political tribes and online arguments have shifted around 2016, and make some predictions.
Why do people hate the group next door more than groups that are totally different from them? It seems backwards.
Someone argued that Western civilization is a hardy weed that's conquering the globe, and that traditionalists underrate it. Is Coca-Cola or 'Western medicine' really Western in any meaningful sense?
How did the Industrial Revolution change the way culture spreads around the world? Why does a philosopher in the 1600s or a blogger today have more in common with distant peers than with neighbors?

Write a short blog post about two kinds of goals, the ones where you want something and build a plan, and the ones where you already have the plan and must find a reason to fill it. Why do the second kind feel off to you?

I'm a psychiatry resident about to start my final year and want to write a funny, honest, slightly rueful blog post about what a year of training changes: the tricks you pick up, the supervisors, the moments of doubt, the things that scare you. Write it as a series of short numbered sections, in a wry first-person voice.
honest question, do therapists actually enjoy doing psychotherapy? I feel like if I were on the other side of the couch I'd feel like a fraud
what's it like being trained in psychodynamic therapy by a supervisor who really believes in it? Is it as annoying as it sounds?
what do people mean by a 'reverse lottery' in medicine, and why is it so easy to fall into playing them?

I keep seeing press releases saying a new study proves something surprising about fathers and sons. Take a recent one like that, look at the actual paper, and write up what you find. I'd like a skeptical statistician's view on what to believe.
why is it a problem to run dozens of subgroup comparisons and then say 'but so many came out significant overall'? Can you give an example with made-up numbers?
why would stress make chronic pain flare up if the pain isn't 'all in your head'? what's the plausible mechanism?

Write an essay arguing against the habit of reading hidden coded messages into politicians' offhand remarks. Use a few recent examples from the 2016 campaign and British politics, and say what you think is lost when 'offensive' gets treated as the same thing as 'bigoted'.
why has the media gotten so into the idea of 'dog whistles'? Is it still tracking anything real?

A new study just showed ketamine's antidepressant effect comes from a metabolite, not the mechanism everyone assumed. I'm wondering what that says about how trustworthy psychiatric research is. Write a blog post digging into how the field behaved before it corrected itself.

Write a speculative essay about an economy that slowly drifts out of human control: companies run by algorithms, owned by algorithms, selling to other algorithms. Could that actually happen, what would stop it, and why should we worry?
could an economy accidentally end up in a self-sustaining loop that has nothing to do with people? like what would that even look like
why are corporations so hard to regulate? they always seem to find a loophole
I just got a copy of Robin Hanson's Age of Em and I'm a little nervous about it. You've read his blog for years, right? What's it actually like to take in a thinker like that?
people who say they're totally fine with whatever values future generations end up having always seem a bit smug to me. is there actually a problem with that attitude?
Can you explain the idea of an economy that eventually runs itself with no humans left, where growth is just for growth's sake? Walk me through how you get from a normal company to that.
Honestly I'm pretty pessimistic that we can fix poverty with better schools and social programs. Am I being lazy or is there real evidence for that gloom?

Headlines keep saying one good fourth-grade teacher can boost your lifetime earnings by tens of thousands of dollars, but I also read that parenting barely matters. How would anyone even test how much teachers matter?
How do researchers decide which teachers are actually good? Why can't you just compare their students' average test scores?

Write an essay about why we tend to sympathize with people in a bad job situation only when we've seen it up close, and whether being personally affected makes someone a better or worse judge of whether they're being treated fairly. Feel free to be honest about your own inconsistencies.
have you ever noticed your political opinions flip the moment something bad actually happened to you personally? like you'd have argued the other side in the abstract

I'm trying to make up my mind about whether junior doctors who strike over their working conditions are justified. You trained in a medical system outside the US and have worked in the American one. Write something honest about what you saw and where you land, including your doubts about labor disputes in general.
Why is being a junior doctor in the US bearable for a lot of people but apparently so much worse in Britain or Ireland? Isn't it the same long hours everywhere?

A biologist argues that you can't engineer smarter humans because every gene touches many systems, so optimizing for intelligence must cost you health or other traits, like a car built only for speed. Is that objection actually right? Write it up carefully, with the evidence and your own uncertainty about the genetics.

I run an online forum and keep getting asked why I ban people who try to publicly shame others, since shaming can be a legitimate social tool. Write an essay on when meanness, if ever, is excusable, and what principle I could use to decide.
Is 'just be nice' a good enough ethical rule? A friend swears it settles every moral question.

Many of the scientists who ran the first psychedelic experiments in the 1950s and 60s went on to hold some extremely strange beliefs. Write an essay speculating on why that happened, and what it might tell us about the drugs. Be upfront about how speculative you are.
Where does religion come from? I'm tired of the usual answers about hyperactive agent detection. Write an essay with a different angle, one that takes ancient religions seriously on their own terms.
is American culture basically a religion? like does it have the same parts, or is that just a cute analogy
Does the Hebrew Bible actually claim other gods don't exist? And how did the Romans think about worshipping gods?

Groups like nations, religions, fandoms, parties and online communities all seem to share some common machinery, whatever they claim to be about. Write an essay on what that shared thing is, why people value belonging to these groups despite the obvious dangers, and why almost any shared activity seems to drift toward becoming a social club.
I used to think tribalism was just plain bad, but lately I find I actually like being part of groups. Is there a real case for it, or am I rationalizing?
Why is it so hard for someone raised in a very religious community to just leave when they stop being sure the beliefs are true?
Honestly, would you rather be homeless or locked in a psychiatric hospital for life? I work near a ward and I keep wondering what patients actually give up when they're admitted.

I've read plenty of self-help success books and never trust them. Someone told me to look at Trump's 1988 book The Art of the Deal, as a how-to on persuasion and success. Write a book review: is there anything to learn from it, and what does it reveal about the man who wrote it?

Twin studies are always summarized as '50% nature, 50% nurture,' and people take the 'nurture' half to mean parenting, schools and friends. Is that reading right? Write a post on what the non-shared environment term in twin studies actually contains.
if identical twins have the same genes and end up with very different incomes, doesn't that mean something about their upbringing must have differed? or could it just be luck?

A Vox piece argues that prisons have become America's substitute for a gutted mental health system, since mentally ill people in prison outnumber those in state hospitals ten to one. As a practicing psychiatrist, write a rebuttal that checks the statistic and the story behind it.
Were the old long-term state mental hospitals actually that much better than prison? People talk about bringing them back.

Online communities that prize open debate seem to get stuck re-fighting the same few arguments forever. Why does that happen, and what can a community do about it without giving up on honest disagreement? I'd like a thoughtful blog post.

You're a psychiatrist reflecting on your own habits. Write an essay on the two broad stances a doctor can take toward what patients say they want, taking them at their word versus looking for the real problem underneath, and which one you lean toward and why.
I'm trying to write about a pretty abstract idea and everyone's eyes glaze over. How do I make a complicated point land in a blog post?
when I write an argument, should I bring up the strongest objections myself or just let the other side raise them? feels like it hands them ammo
Why does writing sound so awkward when sentences keep starting with the same word? But I've seen repetition work well too. What's the difference?

A study came out claiming that women's contributions to open source projects on GitHub get judged differently depending on whether their gender is visible, and the headlines are all about sexism in tech. I haven't read the paper. Can you go through what it actually found, how far the evidence goes, and whether the coverage is fair? Write it up like a blog post from a skeptical statistics-minded reader.

Write a book review of Philip Tetlock's Superforecasting for a blog audience that's already interested in rationality and cognitive biases. Explain what the book claims about people who predict the future unusually well, what to make of it, and how much a reader who knows the field already would get out of it.

Write a blog post about the link between smoking and schizophrenia. I've seen claims that smoking causes psychosis and others that it protects against it, and I'd like someone to dig into how good the evidence on each side actually is, and what researchers should do when studies disagree.
why do so many people with schizophrenia smoke? is it just stress or something more biological?

I work as a psychiatrist and I keep feeling like the world is far more miserable than most people around me seem to think. Help me write an essay on how much hidden suffering there is, why we don't see it, and whether I can check my impression with some rough numbers.
What's it actually like working as a psychiatrist? What kind of lives do your patients have?

OpenAI has just launched with the promise to make advanced AI research open source and widely available. Is that actually a good idea for safety? Write a thoughtful critique that takes the risks of superintelligence seriously.

I just finished a popular-science book arguing that a country's average IQ matters far more for its wealth than any one person's IQ matters for theirs. Write a thoughtful review: lay out the book's case fairly, then say where it's convincing and where it leaves you with questions.

You're a psychiatrist who does couples therapy, and a couple comes in with a conflict that looks genuinely zero-sum: one partner wants to be allowed something the other can't bear. Therapeutic neutrality says you can't take a side, but a friend would. Write an essay on how we should decide who is right in disputes like this, and what that says about the role of culture.

My uncle insists we need college because it teaches you to think critically. Does the evidence actually back that up? Go through what the research shows, how much to trust it, and what we still don't know.

I've been a critic of a certain political movement for years from the margins, and now big mainstream outlets are suddenly piling on with the same complaint. You'd think I'd be pleased. Write an essay about why having the powerful take up your side can be a reason for unease rather than celebration.

Write an essay on developmental psychology for adults: the idea that some ways of thinking, like seeing that other people have different minds, are skills people may never fully pick up rather than stages everyone passes through. What milestones might some adults be missing, and how would you even tell?
What is 'theory of mind' in child development? How do kids go from not getting that other people think differently to getting it, and what else shows up in that age range?

Every few months a headline says some food is as bad as smoking or raises your mortality by 20%. Write a piece on how to make sense of those numbers, using the processed-meat scare as the worked example. I want to know how much it actually matters.
I'm a doctor and a patient refuses a drug that would clearly help her because she read it raises mortality a little. How do you put a small risk in perspective for someone who's scared of it?

Why is it that generic drugs, which are supposed to be the cheap, competitive part of the pharmaceutical market, so often end up weirdly expensive? A drug company just jacked up the price of an old drug 5000% and I want to understand how the system lets that happen. Write it up as a blog post by someone who prescribes these things.
my patient's antidepressant has been generic for ages, so why does the pharmacy price seem to vary so wildly from store to store? any tips?

I think animals have moral value and I also eat meat, and I'm tired of pretending that's not awkward. Write a blog post for fellow meat-eaters about practical ways to cut down the harm we do without going full vegetarian.
if I care about animal suffering but don't want to give up meat, is there any swap that actually makes a big difference?

Write an essay on whether effective altruists should get involved in 'systemic change' and political causes, as critics keep demanding. Take a cautious view if you can make it, and let it work through the objections, maybe as a conversation between two voices.
what's the actual difference between regular charity and 'systemic change' or political causes? why do people treat them so differently?

Write an essay on how journalists and activists can make any group look terrible using only true anecdotes. Maybe try demonstrating it on a profession that doesn't deserve the reputation, and then explain what's wrong with the technique.
what is the 'Chinese robber fallacy'? and why would it matter for how we think about media bias?
A professor wrote in the New York Times that psychology's replication failures are no cause for alarm, just ordinary science at work. Write a response arguing whether that reassurance holds up.
ok but if two careful studies of the same psychology effect get opposite results, why can't we just say the conditions differed slightly? why does that still count as a problem for the field?
why do both the left and the right insist the media is biased against them? is one of them just wrong?
how do US-backed regimes in poor countries tend to slide into death squads and endless violence? is there a typical pattern?
why do outsider candidates seem to be doing so much better lately? is political polarization part of it?

A paper just claimed a blood test can predict suicide risk with 92% accuracy and the press is running with it. I'm a psychiatrist-ish skeptic. Write a blog post picking the claim apart, both whether the study shows it and whether it would matter if true.
if a medical test is 92% accurate, why is a positive result still not that meaningful for something rare like suicide risk? explain with numbers

Write a speculative essay linking hallucinations, paranoia and mystical experience. Is there one cognitive mechanism behind why a broken brain sees things that aren't there and why meditators and prophets report cosmic understanding?

People keep telling me you can't assign probabilities to things when you have no model, like first contact with aliens or a risky long-shot bet. I think that's wrong. Write a piece arguing about whether we can and should use probability without a model.
if I really can't model something, can't I just say I don't know and refuse to put a probability on it? like choosing between a safe grant and a wild long shot

Write a long essay on overconfidence: how sure people say they are versus how often they're right, what saying 'one in a million' really commits you to, and what it should change about how we argue and treat people who disagree.
how overconfident are people actually? is there data on calibration when people say they're 99% sure?
people say 'the majority is always wrong' and it sounds dumb but is there any sense in which it could be true?

I've been getting defensive online lately and a friend asked why. Write a candid piece explaining, from the gut, why criticism that aims to make a group disreputable can doom it, and why that makes someone jumpy.
what's the difference between real criticism and the kind of online argument that just tries to make a group look disgusting? how does that work?

A critic says the case for funding existential-risk work depends on made-up probabilities that you can shrink by adding zeroes until the argument fails. Write a response on when it is legitimate to put tiny numbers on things and why the zeroes aren't free.
how do you avoid being a gullible believer in whatever the experts say without turning into a conspiracy theorist? it feels like fixing one error just causes the other

Why do people who turn out to be right against the scientific consensus so rarely get credit for it, while cranks get dismissed loudly? I'd like a thoughtful essay on telling real contrarians from crackpots, and what happens to the contrarians even when they win.
People say 'the scientific consensus' like it's one thing. Who is actually included in that? Can you break it down for me?
how do paradigm shifts actually happen in science? Like what does it look like on the ground before somebody proposes the new idea

I keep noticing that some careers (medicine, academia, big law) are all-or-nothing while others like programming are smooth ladders. Write a blog post about what makes a field like that, whether it's unhealthy, and where else the pattern shows up.

Is there such a thing as being generally good at getting answers right, across unrelated controversial questions, independent of IQ or just agreeing with experts? Write it up as an essay for a rationalist-leaning blog, considering what evidence would show it and why it matters.

Libertarians like to say that competition between private communities, each trying to offer the best rules, will protect freedom better than government can. The internet looks like a real-world test of that idea. Write an essay on whether it actually has, especially for unpopular speech.

Cognitive-behavioral therapy seems to work less well in recent studies than it did in the 1980s. I'm a psychiatry trainee reading a CBT self-help book full of dramatic success stories, and the results I see in real life look nothing like them. Write a speculative, thinking-out-loud blog post about why the effect might be shrinking.

People increasingly appeal to 'cultural evolution' to argue that traditions we inherited must be doing something useful, even if we can't see what. Write an essay on whether that argument actually holds up, and what different things the phrase can mean.

I just read a news story about a woman who says she was wrongly committed to a psych ward for claiming a famous person follows her on social media. You work as a psychiatrist. Write a blog post giving the view from inside the system on whether this was as outrageous as it sounds.
why is it so hard for psychiatrists to decide whether to believe what a patient tells them? like, why not just check?

I'm a psychiatry resident and just hit the halfway mark of my four years. Write a reflective blog post about what I've learned working inpatient, what the work does to you, and what I'm wondering about as I move to outpatient.
is it true that psychiatric hospitals are total chaos like in the movies? what's it actually like inside one?
why do people get sent to a psych ward for like a week when meds take weeks to work? what is the hospital actually doing for them?

Write an essay about whether making college free is the right response to the way degrees have become required for everything. I'd like you to use an analogy or a story to get at the problem, and bring in some real examples from jobs people actually do.
Can you tell me a short parable about a government that subsidizes something whose price has been bid up by outside speculation, and what ends up happening?
do doctors in the US actually need a four-year undergrad degree before med school? Ireland seems to skip it, so what do we get for the extra years?

A journalist ran a deliberately bad diet study and got the press to report that chocolate helps you lose weight. Everyone online is drawing big lessons from it about science, statistics and the media. Write a blog post sorting out which of those lessons are right and which are overreactions.
how does nutrition science ever get to a trustworthy answer if you can't run the perfect experiment? like, every single study seems to have some flaw

I've noticed that when I compare political candidates or weigh up causes, I tend to treat every issue as equally weighty. Is there a good metaphor from how the US Congress is built for what's wrong with that kind of reasoning? Write it up as a short essay.
why does the US have both a House and a Senate, and why do they represent states differently? explain the history for someone who isn't American

Imagine that in ten years, machine-learning filters let everyone block anything they don't want to see online, down to whole categories of speech. Write an essay thinking through what that would do to public argument and to who holds power. Draw on today's tools like keyword blockers and shared block lists.

I'm a psychiatry resident and I've been poking around online drug-review sites, where patients rate their medications. Write a blog post about what you might learn by comparing patient ratings with doctors' ratings and with how often drugs get prescribed. Be honest about what could be confounding the numbers.

Why do doctors avoid prescribing drugs with rare but dramatic side effects, even when the alternatives hurt more people in quieter ways? Write it up as a blog post by someone working in psychiatry, with concrete examples and some rough numbers.

I want a blog post about how to read a scientific paper skeptically when the abstract sounds too good. Use a recent psychology study on student mindset interventions as the worked example, and show how an impressive abstract can hide weak results.
how do you find the weak spots in a field where everybody seems to believe the same thing and nobody publishes the other side?

Academics from privileged backgrounds often seem eager to blame their own group for the world's problems, which looks odd. Write a short essay proposing a psychological explanation that is charitable rather than cynical.
why would people latch onto the idea that Western countries caused global poverty even when the evidence is shaky? is there a more generous explanation than status-signaling?

Two well-designed experiments on whether academic hiring committees favor men or women just came out with opposite results, and each side is citing its own. How should a sensible person think about that? Write it as a blog post, and be willing to speculate about why the studies differ.
do you buy the whole growth mindset thing? I feel like it's too good to be true but I can't put my finger on why

Someone told me superintelligent AI can't be dangerous because it's just software on a computer with no way to touch the physical world. Write an essay answering that objection. Assume a skeptical but smart reader.
ok but concretely, how would an AI with no body ever actually take control of a country? give me a plausible scenario

Lately it's fashionable to say psychiatry lied to the public with the 'chemical imbalance' theory of depression. You're a psychiatry resident who thinks that charge is mostly unfair. Write a long essay defending your profession and explaining what the phrase actually meant and why it was said.
Why does alcohol, which acts like a calming brain chemical, sometimes make people angry and anxious instead of relaxed? Doesn't that mean the neuroscience is wrong?

If a disease has a long chain of causes, is it wrong for a doctor to give just one of them as 'the cause'? Like if someone says a condition is caused by a chemical imbalance, is that a fraud if it's incomplete?
As a psychiatrist, how do you handle families who think a depressed person is just lazy or not trying? Do you explain the science?

A TV personality got into trouble for describing a grotesque hypothetical to make a point about atheists and morality, and everyone's outraged. As someone with a philosophy background, how do you think about extreme, disturbing thought experiments in general? Are they just morbid, or is there a real method to them? Write it as a blog post.
why do philosophers always use such extreme examples in thought experiments, like murderers at the door? why not something realistic

People keep claiming that environmentalism, social justice, transhumanism, even Apple fandom is 'really a religion'. Is that a meaningful claim or a cheap rhetorical move? Write an essay working out what, if anything, is going on.

I get the arguments for anarcho-capitalism and even find them clever, but something about it bugs me at a more basic level. Is there a good outside-view reason to be skeptical that 'just don't use force' solves governance?

Some psychology studies claim huge, lasting effects from tiny interventions, while expensive multi-year social programs barely move the needle. What should we make of that gap? Write a short, skeptical blog post.

Why do small online communities and hobby groups so often get stuck at the same size no matter how hard they recruit? Write an essay drawing on personal experience, and be honest about how much you trust any neat theory of it.

I want a blog post about what happens when you take utilitarianism seriously at a meetup and someone pushes you on animal welfare. How do you stay sane while still being honest about your own inconsistency?

Genetics people say childhood interventions barely matter; psychiatrists say they matter hugely. Take one good randomized trial of early intervention and tell me what to make of it, both scientifically and as policy.

Everyone assumes doctors who take drug company money are shady. Write a funny, honest piece from a psychiatry resident's perspective on how pharma influence actually works on people who think they're ethical.
Could the long decline in testosterone help explain why crime fell? Look at the evidence, poke holes in the idea, and say what data you'd want.
Write a piece about psychiatric hospital work from a resident's view: the kinds of patients who really show up, and one case that made you rethink what we spend money on.

Headlines say drug testing welfare applicants found almost no drug users. Dig into whether those numbers mean what the media says, and what it says about honesty in journalism when you're on the right side of an argument.

A magazine article says polyamory has a problem because black people are underrepresented in it. Write a response from someone in the poly community, thinking about why any group might be demographically skewed and what the framing does.

Write a satirical New York Times style op-ed from the year 2065 where a smug bioethicist declares that refusing a certain universal medical enhancement for your kids is child abuse. Make it read like real moralizing editorial prose.
Use basketball and height to think clearly about intelligence and talent. What does the NBA height distribution teach us about innate ability versus practice?

Weird thing I've noticed: when people argue about weight, depression, or poverty, being compassionate seems to mean saying it's biological or luck. But with intelligence the sides seem to flip. Is that real, and what do you make of it?
I feel pretty mediocre next to the people doing impressive things in my field. Is there any way to think about that which isn't just 'work harder' or 'be happy with less'?
Where does the word 'talent' actually come from, and does the origin say anything about how we should think about natural ability?
why do online ads take forever to disappear after you hit the X? it drives me nuts
My friends keep arguing about whether humans evolved from monkeys or chimps or apes. Who's actually right?

Newspapers love to point out that places like Denmark and Finland have high antidepressant use and suicide rates, as if that proves they are secretly dysfunctional. Write an essay on what depression and suicide statistics can and can't tell us about how well a society works.

Why does society keep finding new groups it's apparently fine to mock, and why does it seem like each new kind of evil is invisible until it's too late? Write a blog post exploring this, with an idea that ties the two together.
Why would a new Nazi movement have a much harder time winning people over than the original did?
Is weight gain really just 'calories in, calories out'? Write something that takes the thermodynamics seriously but also looks at what the research says about metabolism, genes and willpower.

I keep noticing that a lot of conversation seems to carry no information at all, small talk, the same radio rant every week, stock interview answers, therapists' stock phrases. Write an essay on what that kind of talk is for, and why some people find it comforting and others infuriating.
what is small talk actually for? like when someone asks 'how are you' and nobody means anything by it

Why do arguments about who is the brave dissenter and who is the conformist go so sour so quickly? Write an essay on this pattern in political and cultural debate, including why both sides can be so sure they're the underdog.
why do online arguments get so nasty when people start claiming they're the brave ones going against the mainstream?
Write a deadpan, tongue-in-cheek essay that treats morality as if it were a physical force, with real-sounding calculations, and uses it to explain why we feel less obligated to distant strangers.
Some questions, like whether Mozart is better than Beethoven, seem neither purely subjective nor purely objective. Write a blog post proposing a way to think about this and a word for it.
is 'Mozart is better than Beethoven' just a matter of opinion? but then it feels weird to say the same about Mozart vs a toddler banging on a toy piano

I've been wondering why people think of atheists as loud and angry. Write a short blog post exploring whether that stereotype could come from how we notice groups, and whether it generalizes to other groups.
Many people object to putting numbers on things we can't really measure, like how bad North Korea is to live in or the chance your laptop dies. Write a post defending using made-up numbers anyway.

Write a skeptical but enthusiastic blog post reviewing a psychology paper that tried to use a reaction-time test to predict suicide risk, covering what it claims, what's wrong with it, and why the idea still matters.

if you had to boil down what a long-running fictional-country simulation taught you about power and leadership, what would it be? Even half-joking advice is fine

Write a short blog post praising a favorite debating trick: attacking an argument by showing it would also prove obviously false things. Explain why it's so effective in a time-limited debate and give a few examples.
People keep telling me we should just trust our moral intuitions instead of doing moral philosophy. Is there a good reply to that?

Write an essay about why survey and poll results on weird or extreme beliefs are less trustworthy than they look. Use the headline claim that a few percent of Americans believe lizard people run the world as a starting point, and bring in a couple of other cases where noise or mischief corrupted the data.
I keep seeing headlines that 4% of Americans believe lizard people run the world. Do people really believe that, or is something else going on?

I always found the history of philosophy frustrating because so much of what's taught is obviously wrong by now. Is there still a good reason to read old philosophers? Write a thoughtful piece on how to get value out of them.

Write a witty, critical review of Alasdair MacIntyre's After Virtue from the point of view of a utilitarian-leaning reader who found the book more confusing than convincing, while still giving it a fair hearing.

I've started to doubt utilitarianism as a foundation for ethics. Write an exploratory essay about whether it can really give morality an objective basis or whether it just formalizes our own intuitions, and what might take its place.
Does utilitarianism really say we should prefer a world of people permanently wireheaded on pleasure? Why does that bother me so much, and what does it say about my ethics?

I recently started a polyamorous relationship, and what surprised me most is how ordinary it feels. Write a candid personal essay for skeptical readers about what that experience is actually like, covering the usual objections about love, jealousy, and sex.
Isn't polyamory basically just a way to have lots of sex with lots of people? Honest answer, please.

I just got back from a talk on effective charity where one of the speakers argued that donors are mostly fooling themselves. Write me a blog post about what it's like to hear that, and whether the idea of investing your money now and giving it away later actually holds up. Do some back-of-the-envelope math.

When I was in college I devoured books on mysticism and the occult, and I think it did me more harm than good. Write an essay on the difference between learning about a field and actually learning it, and why that trap is especially bad for spiritual stuff.

A friend says the cure for youth unemployment is abolishing the minimum wage so everyone can find some job. Write a blog post taking that seriously and then arguing the strongest case you can for why it might backfire, especially as automation advances.

Do we pick partners who are genetically similar to us or different from us? Write it up as a curious, slightly meandering blog post: lay out the evidence on both sides, including the weird stuff, and be honest about where the explanation falls apart.

I've just finished Infinite Jest and I'm still puzzled. Write a long, funny, opinionated review for people who've read it (spoilers fine) that tries to say what the book is actually about and how its structure relates to that.

I'm starting a blog with no single subject and want to open with a short statement of the attitude I'll bring to disagreement. Write that first post for me, with a bit of humor but a real point about how to treat ideas you think are wrong.
